chunk_findings.detail: `instants` clamps the sampling interval with `step = max(float(step_s), 1.0)` (line 31) and spaces the returned instants by that clamped `step`, but `sample` never learns about the clamp: it reports `"step_s": m.grid_step_s` verbatim (lines 46 and 72) and uses the unclamped `m.grid_step_s` for the lease-event lookback window, `stamped[bisect_left(times, t - m.grid_step_s) : upto]` (line 57). So for any configured value the clamp actually anticipates (`[metrics] grid_step_s = 0`, or any value below 1), the rows come out 1.0 s apart while being labelled `step_s = 0`, and the lookback window becomes `[t, t]` instead of one step wide. Concretely: with `grid_step_s = 0` and a log where an agent acquired and released a lease between two sample instants, `recent` is empty at every instant (the slice `bisect_left(times, t) : bisect_right(times, t)` contains only events timestamped exactly at `t`), so `lanes == working` always, `lanes - working == 0`, `idle_with_ready` sums to 0, and `utilisation` (line 85) returns `working / working == 1.0` — i.e. 100 % utilisation regardless of how many lanes sat idle, plus a `step_s` field that any consumer such as B-af-headroom will bucket against and silently get wrong. The clamp needs to be applied once and the clamped value returned/used, or `sample` must reject/round the configured step itself.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/grid.py:31 (with :57 and :72)

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring of `dur` states the invariant "(a figure never reads 0)", but the minutes branch `f"{seconds / minute:.0f}m"` rounds to zero for any duration under 30 seconds, so the guarantee does not hold. Concrete inputs: `dur(0.0)` returns `"0m"`, `dur(20.0)` returns `"0m"`, and `dur(29.0)` returns `"0m"`. This is directly reachable in normal output — `retro` renders the first timeline entry with `r.get('offset_s', 0.0)` (line ~76), which is 0 for the claim event, so every retro prints `+0m  ...`, and any short queue wait / lease wait / gate time (all passed through `_stat` -> `dur`) is displayed as `0m` instead of a non-zero figure, defeating the stated "a figure never reads 0" intent. The same rounding also turns 30-59.9 s into `"1m"` and 3599 s into `"60m"`, so the branch boundary is not handled cleanly either. The underlying JSON is unaffected, but the human text is the deliverable for these views and can report zero for a non-zero measured wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:14-18 (`dur`)

chunk_findings.detail: The early-return guard is evaluated *before* the "ready (dependencies done)" row is appended, so it tests for "at least two own events" rather than the "readiness alone is no story" condition its own comment describes. Given an item whose only own step is `lease.acquired` and whose span has a `ready_at` (i.e. the ordinary "claimed, still in flight / abandoned" case), `rows` holds exactly one entry, `rows[1:]` is empty, and the function returns `{"entries": [claim], "gaps": [], "biggest_gap": None, "total_s": None}` writing off the whole timeline. The `ready` marker is never added, so the ready→claim gap — precisely the queue wait the service advertises ("queue wait (ready->claimed)") and frequently the largest contributor to a slow item — is dropped, and the biggest gap is never named. Moving the ready append above the guard (or making the guard `if not rows`) yields `[ready, claim]`, one gap, and the correct `biggest_gap`/`total_s` for that same input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/retro.py:68 (`timeline`, guard `if not rows[1:]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `--phase` guard validates the phase name against `state.items`, the same mapping that the `retro` branch two blocks below validates an item id against (`if item not in state.items`). A single mapping cannot be keyed by both item ids (`B-rm-changes`) and workflow phase names (`build`, `docs`, …) unless every phase name happened to also be an item id, so at least one of the two checks is looking at the wrong collection. Concretely, `ddflow metrics --phase docs` (or `ddflow forecast --phase docs`) on a log that has plenty of items in the `docs` phase and no item literally named `docs` takes the line-76/77 branch and returns `Answer(False, "no phase 'docs'", failed=True)` — the command fails instead of filtering, so the whole `--phase` flag is unusable for every real phase name. The check needs to test against the set of phases actually present in `state` (e.g. `state.phases`, or the distinct `item.phase` values) rather than the item-id keyed `state.items`.

chunk_findings.detail: `reasons = Counter(" ".join(o.reason.split())[:100] or "(no reason)" for o in skipped)` calls `.split()` on the raw `o.reason` before the fallback can apply. The `or "(no reason)"` shows the author expects skips without a reason (the sibling `o.by or "(unknown)"` guards the same kind of missing field), but a missing reason is normally encoded as `None`, not `""`. Given a skip outcome with `reason=None` (a `gate skip` event logged with no justification — exactly the case the fallback is written for), `None.split()` raises `AttributeError` and the whole `ddflow metrics` skip audit aborts instead of tallying that skip under `"(no reason)"`; the fallback only ever fires for whitespace-only strings. The guard must be moved before the call, e.g. `(o.reason or "").split()`, so that missing reasons are bucketed rather than crashing the report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/skips.py:24 (`_gate_row`, the `reasons = Counter(...)` line)

chunk_findings.detail: `has_figures` decides exit 2 ("not enough data") by checking only `cycle_time`, `gate_time`, `review_rounds`, `rework`, `outcomes` and `providers`; it omits the two figures the same `build` computes into the returned dict: `queue_wait` and `lease_wait`. Its own docstring says "Whether any figure at all could be computed (else the answer is exit 2)", so this is self-inconsistent. Concrete input: a log where N ≥ `[metrics] min_samples` items have a dated `ready_at` and a `first_claim` (so `queue_waits(ctx)` yields N samples and `need("queue_wait", ...)` produces a real `p50_s`), but none of those items has completed (`cycle_s` is None, so `completed_spans` is empty) and no gate verdict has been recorded for them. Then `completed_spans`/`review_rounds` are empty, `gate_time`, `rework` and `outcomes` are all unavailable, and `has_figures` returns False, so the command exits 2 "not enough data" even though a computed queue-wait (and lease-wait) figure with sufficient samples exists in `data`. The same holds when the only supported figure is `lease_wait`. `has_figures` should also consult `data["queue_wait"]["p50_s"]` and `data["lease_wait"]["p50_s"]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py:has_figures

chunk_findings.detail: The help topic — which ACCEPTANCE names as a deliverable ("README + help topic") — documents the forecast, retro, skip-audit and lanes views as subcommands of `ddflow metrics` (`ddflow metrics forecast`, `ddflow metrics retro <id>`, `ddflow metrics skips`, `ddflow metrics lanes`), whereas the interface this change is specified against is the top-level set `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`, `ddflow retro <id>`, plus the skip audit ("One log-derived metrics service: ddflow metrics, forecast … and retro <id>"; "`ddflow forecast [--phase P]`"; "`ddflow retro <id>`"; "the three commands work on CLI and MCP"). The two surfaces cannot both be right: a user who follows the stated acceptance criterion and types `ddflow forecast --phase P` gets an unknown-command error if the help reflects the CLI, and a user who follows the help and types `ddflow metrics forecast` gets one if the CLI is the three top-level commands. Since the help is the only user-facing description of the command surface shipped here, it must be brought in line with whatever the implemented CLI/MCP entry points actually are (the MCP side already collapses everything into `ddflow_metrics` with `view` = summary/forecast/retro/skips/lanes, which is not what the CLI section of this file suggests).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/metrics.md:11-15

chunk_findings.detail: `_percent` returns the success value for a boolean because `bool` is a subclass of `int`: `_percent(True)` evaluates `isinstance(True, int) and True in range(1, 100)` → `True`, so it returns `""` (accepted). With config `forecast_high_pct = true` the check passes and the high percentile is taken as 1, while `forecast_low_pct` stays at its default 50, yielding an inverted, nonsensical range instead of the "not a percentile between 1 and 99" rejection the check exists to produce. A stricter type guard (e.g. rejecting `bool` before the range test) is needed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/metrics.py `_percent` / `forecast_low_pct`, `forecast_high_pct`

chunk_findings.detail: The guard tests the `--phase` value for membership in `state.items`, which is the item-id mapping (the very next lines index it as `state.items[i]` to get a chain node's kind, and `_empty_reason` scopes a phase with the separate `state.tasks(phase)` filter). A phase is a pipeline stage/filter, not an item id: `ddflow forecast --phase docs-stage` evaluates `"docs-stage" not in state.items` to True and immediately returns `{"available": False, "reason": "no phase 'docs-stage'"}` before `critical_path`/`state.tasks` are ever consulted, so a perfectly valid phase never yields a P50/P90 range. The fact that the guard rejects the value as "no phase" while the code two functions below uses `state.tasks(phase)` to enumerate that same phase's work shows the existence test is looking in the wrong namespace; it should use the phase scope (e.g. `state.tasks(phase)` / the phase registry), not the item-id keys.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/metrics/forecast.py:86 (`forecast`, the `if phase and phase not in state.items:` guard)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/forecast.py:86 (`forecast`, the `if phase and phase not in state.items:` guard)

chunk_findings.detail:
`dur` formats every duration strictly below an hour as `f"{seconds / minute:.0f}m"`. Because of that `:.0f` rounding, any nonzero duration under 30 seconds collapses to the literal string `0m`, which directly contradicts the function's own stated contract — "(a figure never reads 0)". Concretely, `dur(20)` returns `"0m"`, `dur(0)` returns `"0m"`, and `dur(29)` returns `"0m"`. This is not a hypothetical: `dur` is the formatter for gate times (`_stat` with the default `fmt=dur`) and for every timeline offset in `retro`, including `r.get('offset_s', 0.0)`, where the first event is emitted with offset 0. So a fast gate whose p50 is 20 s is reported as `p50 0m`, and a sub-30 s wait in the retro timeline prints `+0m` — the reader cannot distinguish "instantaneous" from "twenty seconds", and the metric asserts a nonzero measured duration is zero. The unit threshold would need a seconds branch (or a floor of one second) for the documented invariant to hold.

No violation of the supplied guidance records (`D-rules-format`, `D-rules-hierarchy`) is implicated by this rendering-only change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:14 (`dur`)

chunk_findings.detail: The early-return guard is evaluated against the item's own `STEP` events *before* the readiness entry is appended, so it is broader than its comment ("readiness alone is no story"). Given an item whose only own `STEPS` event is, say, `item.blocked` (or `lease.acquired`) while `facts.spans[item].ready_at` is set, `own` yields exactly one row, `rows[1:]` is empty, and the function returns `{"entries": [<one row>], "gaps": [], "biggest_gap": None, "total_s": None}` without ever adding the `"ready (dependencies done)"` row. The single readiness→event gap — the whole wait for that item, i.e. the answer to "why was this slow" that the docstring and acceptance criteria promise — is silently discarded even though it is computable. The guard needs to be applied to the rows *including* the readiness entry (or be `if not rows:` plus a post-insert length check), not to `own` alone; the current form only guarantees `len(rows) >= 2` for items that already have two or more own step events.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/retro.py:66 (`if not rows[1:]:`)

chunk_findings.detail: The phase guard validates the `--phase` value against `state.items` — the very mapping that `retro` uses to look up an *item* id (`if item not in state.items` two branches later). Items and phases are distinct concepts in this design (items have cycle times; a phase is the pipeline stage used to filter them). Concretely, given `ddflow metrics --phase build` (or any real phase name), `phase not in state.items` is evaluated against item ids, so it never matches and the command returns `Answer(False, "no phase 'build'", failed=True)` — exit 2 — even though the phase exists and `facts`/`Context` are ready to filter on it. The check needs the set of phases actually present in the folded log (or pipeline config), not the item-id map. As written, the documented `[--phase P]` interface of `metrics` (and the same guard run for `forecast`) rejects every legitimate phase name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: `Counter(" ".join(o.reason.split())[:100] or "(no reason)" for o in skipped)` calls `o.reason.split()` before the `or "(no reason)"` fallback can run. A skip outcome whose reason is absent (`None`) — the natural representation for a log-derived fact recorded without a reason — raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split'`, so the entire `ddflow metrics` / MCP skip audit fails on one reason-less skip instead of falling back to `(no reason)`. The same function guards the other nullable field (`o.by or "(unknown)"`) with `or`, so the None case was clearly meant to be handled for `reason` too; the written fallback only covers the empty/whitespace-only string case (`"".split()` → `" ".join([])` → `""`), which is why it looks correct but is not. Concrete input: a single skip fact with `reason=None` (e.g., a `gate skip` recorded without a reason, or an older log entry) makes `audit(ctx)` raise while building `gates`, before any output is produced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/skips.py `_gate_row` (reasons line)

chunk_findings.detail: `review_rounds` builds its counter directly over `ctx.facts.outcomes` instead of `scoped_outcomes(ctx)`, so the per-item review-round figure is the item's *entire* history even when the view is narrowed by `--since`/`--phase`. Every other consumer of outcomes in this file narrows first (`outcome_table` uses `scoped_outcomes(ctx)`; `gate_durations` explicitly checks `ctx.in_scope(o.item, o.at)`), so the same verdict can be counted in `review_rounds` while being dropped from `outcomes` and `gate_time`. Concrete case: `ddflow metrics --since 2026-01-01` on a log where item X completes on 2026-01-02 but its three `rubber_duck` verdicts were all recorded on 2025-12-30 — `review_rounds` returns 3 for X (and the P50 is computed over that), while `outcome_table` counts zero of those verdicts and `gate_durations` yields no duration for them, producing a report whose review-round figure is inconsistent with the rest of the view and inflated by out-of-window history. The fix is to build `counts` from the same in-scope outcome set the other readers use.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py:60-62 (`review_rounds`)

Since the help is the only user-facing description of the command surface shipped here, it must be brought in line with whatever the implemented CLI/MCP entry points actually are (the MCP side already collapses everything into `ddflow_metrics` with `view` = summary/forecast/retro/skips/lanes, which is not what the CLI section of this file suggests).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/metrics.md:11-15

chunk_findings.detail: The only protection against a zero step was inside the shared helper: `step = max(float(step_s), 1.0)` became `step = float(step_s)`. `grid()` now clamps on its own path (`step = max(float(m.grid_step_s), 1.0)`), so the grid command is fine, but `instants()` is the public, documented helper (`instants(first, now, step_s, max_folds, since)`) that other consumers of this sampler call with the configured step. Given `instants(t0, now, 0.0, 24, None)` — reachable because `grid_step_s` is exactly the kind of value the clamp existed to defend against — the very next line computes `int((now - start) // step)`, i.e. `// 0.0`, and raises `ZeroDivisionError`; before this change the same call returned a grid spaced at 1s. Any out-of-module caller that passes `m.grid_step_s` straight through now crashes instead of sampling.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/grid.py:31 (`instants`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The new test's assertion is malformed by Python operator precedence and cannot exercise what its name claims. `==` binds tighter than `and`, so

    assert _percent(True) and _percent(0) and _percent(100) and _percent(90) == ""

is evaluated as

    assert _percent(True) and _percent(0) and _percent(100) and (_percent(90) == "")

i.e. the emptiness check landed on `90`, not on the boolean. For the assert to pass you would need `_percent(90) == ""` (a valid percentile rendered as empty) while `_percent(0)`, `_percent(100)` and `_percent(True)` are all truthy — mutually contradictory for any plausible implementation of a percent validator/converter:
- if invalid values return `""`/`None` (the behaviour the test name wants), `_percent(True)` is falsy and the chain short-circuits to `""`, so the assert fails;
- if valid values are returned as non-empty strings/numbers, `_percent(90) != ""`, so the final comparison is `False` and the assert fails;
- if `_percent` returns the raw number, `_percent(0)` is falsy and the assert fails.

So this test either always fails (CI red) or, if it somehow passed, would be asserting that `90` is not a percentile. The intended check was almost certainly `_percent(True) == "" and _percent(0) and _percent(100) and _percent(90)`. Repro: run `pytest tests/test_metrics.py::test_a_bool_is_not_a_percentile` — the boolean-rejection path is never actually tested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_metrics.py::test_a_bool_is_not_a_percentile

chunk_findings.detail: `_percent` returns the success value for a boolean because `bool` is a subclass of `int`: `_percent(True)` evaluates `isinstance(True, int) and True in range(1, 100)` → `True`, so it returns `""` (accepted). With config `forecast_high_pct = true` the check passes and the high percentile is taken as 1, while `forecast_low_pct` stays at its default 50, yielding an inverted, nonsensical range instead of the "not a percentile between 1 and 99" rejection the check exists to produce. A stricter type guard (e.g. rejecting `bool` before the range test) is needed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/metrics.py `_percent` / `forecast_low_pct`, `forecast_high_pct`

chunk_findings.detail: The guard tests the `--phase` value for membership in `state.items`, which is the item-id mapping (the very next lines index it as `state.items[i]` to get a chain node's kind, and `_empty_reason` scopes a phase with the separate `state.tasks(phase)` filter). A phase is a pipeline stage/filter, not an item id: `ddflow forecast --phase docs-stage` evaluates `"docs-stage" not in state.items` to True and immediately returns `{"available": False, "reason": "no phase 'docs-stage'"}` before `critical_path`/`state.tasks` are ever consulted, so a perfectly valid phase never yields a P50/P90 range. The fact that the guard rejects the value as "no phase" while the code two functions below uses `state.tasks(phase)` to enumerate that same phase's work shows the existence test is looking in the wrong namespace; it should use the phase scope (e.g. `state.tasks(phase)` / the phase registry), not the item-id keys.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/metrics/forecast.py:86 (`forecast`, the `if phase and phase not in state.items:` guard)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/forecast.py:86 (`forecast`, the `if phase and phase not in state.items:` guard)

chunk_findings.detail:
`dur` formats every duration strictly below an hour as `f"{seconds / minute:.0f}m"`. Because of that `:.0f` rounding, any nonzero duration under 30 seconds collapses to the literal string `0m`, which directly contradicts the function's own stated contract — "(a figure never reads 0)". Concretely, `dur(20)` returns `"0m"`, `dur(0)` returns `"0m"`, and `dur(29)` returns `"0m"`. This is not a hypothetical: `dur` is the formatter for gate times (`_stat` with the default `fmt=dur`) and for every timeline offset in `retro`, including `r.get('offset_s', 0.0)`, where the first event is emitted with offset 0. So a fast gate whose p50 is 20 s is reported as `p50 0m`, and a sub-30 s wait in the retro timeline prints `+0m` — the reader cannot distinguish "instantaneous" from "twenty seconds", and the metric asserts a nonzero measured duration is zero. The unit threshold would need a seconds branch (or a floor of one second) for the documented invariant to hold.

No violation of the supplied guidance records (`D-rules-format`, `D-rules-hierarchy`) is implicated by this rendering-only change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:14 (`dur`)

chunk_findings.detail: The early-return guard is evaluated against the item's own `STEP` events *before* the readiness entry is appended, so it is broader than its comment ("readiness alone is no story"). Given an item whose only own `STEPS` event is, say, `item.blocked` (or `lease.acquired`) while `facts.spans[item].ready_at` is set, `own` yields exactly one row, `rows[1:]` is empty, and the function returns `{"entries": [<one row>], "gaps": [], "biggest_gap": None, "total_s": None}` without ever adding the `"ready (dependencies done)"` row. The single readiness→event gap — the whole wait for that item, i.e. the answer to "why was this slow" that the docstring and acceptance criteria promise — is silently discarded even though it is computable. The guard needs to be applied to the rows *including* the readiness entry (or be `if not rows:` plus a post-insert length check), not to `own` alone; the current form only guarantees `len(rows) >= 2` for items that already have two or more own step events.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/retro.py:66 (`if not rows[1:]:`)

chunk_findings.detail: The phase guard validates the `--phase` value against `state.items` — the very mapping that `retro` uses to look up an *item* id (`if item not in state.items` two branches later). Items and phases are distinct concepts in this design (items have cycle times; a phase is the pipeline stage used to filter them). Concretely, given `ddflow metrics --phase build` (or any real phase name), `phase not in state.items` is evaluated against item ids, so it never matches and the command returns `Answer(False, "no phase 'build'", failed=True)` — exit 2 — even though the phase exists and `facts`/`Context` are ready to filter on it. The check needs the set of phases actually present in the folded log (or pipeline config), not the item-id map. As written, the documented `[--phase P]` interface of `metrics` (and the same guard run for `forecast`) rejects every legitimate phase name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: `Counter(" ".join(o.reason.split())[:100] or "(no reason)" for o in skipped)` calls `o.reason.split()` before the `or "(no reason)"` fallback can run. A skip outcome whose reason is absent (`None`) — the natural representation for a log-derived fact recorded without a reason — raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split'`, so the entire `ddflow metrics` / MCP skip audit fails on one reason-less skip instead of falling back to `(no reason)`. The same function guards the other nullable field (`o.by or "(unknown)"`) with `or`, so the None case was clearly meant to be handled for `reason` too; the written fallback only covers the empty/whitespace-only string case (`"".split()` → `" ".join([])` → `""`), which is why it looks correct but is not. Concrete input: a single skip fact with `reason=None` (e.g., a `gate skip` recorded without a reason, or an older log entry) makes `audit(ctx)` raise while building `gates`, before any output is produced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/skips.py `_gate_row` (reasons line)

chunk_findings.detail: `review_rounds` builds its counter directly over `ctx.facts.outcomes` instead of `scoped_outcomes(ctx)`, so the per-item review-round figure is the item's *entire* history even when the view is narrowed by `--since`/`--phase`. Every other consumer of outcomes in this file narrows first (`outcome_table` uses `scoped_outcomes(ctx)`; `gate_durations` explicitly checks `ctx.in_scope(o.item, o.at)`), so the same verdict can be counted in `review_rounds` while being dropped from `outcomes` and `gate_time`. Concrete case: `ddflow metrics --since 2026-01-01` on a log where item X completes on 2026-01-02 but its three `rubber_duck` verdicts were all recorded on 2025-12-30 — `review_rounds` returns 3 for X (and the P50 is computed over that), while `outcome_table` counts zero of those verdicts and `gate_durations` yields no duration for them, producing a report whose review-round figure is inconsistent with the rest of the view and inflated by out-of-window history. The fix is to build `counts` from the same in-scope outcome set the other readers use.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py:60-62 (`review_rounds`)

chunk_findings.detail: `instants` clamps the sampling interval with `step = max(float(step_s), 1.0)` (line 31) and spaces the returned instants by that clamped `step`, but `sample` never learns about the clamp: it reports `"step_s": m.grid_step_s` verbatim (lines 46 and 72) and uses the unclamped `m.grid_step_s` for the lease-event lookback window, `stamped[bisect_left(times, t - m.grid_step_s) : upto]` (line 57). So for any configured value the clamp actually anticipates (`[metrics] grid_step_s = 0`, or any value below 1), the rows come out 1.0 s apart while being labelled `step_s = 0`, and the lookback window becomes `[t, t]` instead of one step wide. Concretely: with `grid_step_s = 0` and a log where an agent acquired and released a lease between two sample instants, `recent` is empty at every instant (the slice `bisect_left(times, t) : bisect_right(times, t)` contains only events timestamped exactly at `t`), so `lanes == working` always, `lanes - working == 0`, `idle_with_ready` sums to 0, and `utilisation` (line 85) returns `working / working == 1.0` — i.e. 100 % utilisation regardless of how many lanes sat idle, plus a `step_s` field that any consumer such as B-af-headroom will bucket against and silently get wrong. The clamp needs to be applied once and the clamped value returned/used, or `sample` must reject/round the configured step itself.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/grid.py:31 (with :57 and :72)

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring of `dur` states the invariant "(a figure never reads 0)", but the minutes branch `f"{seconds / minute:.0f}m"` rounds to zero for any duration under 30 seconds, so the guarantee does not hold. Concrete inputs: `dur(0.0)` returns `"0m"`, `dur(20.0)` returns `"0m"`, and `dur(29.0)` returns `"0m"`. This is directly reachable in normal output — `retro` renders the first timeline entry with `r.get('offset_s', 0.0)` (line ~76), which is 0 for the claim event, so every retro prints `+0m  ...`, and any short queue wait / lease wait / gate time (all passed through `_stat` -> `dur`) is displayed as `0m` instead of a non-zero figure, defeating the stated "a figure never reads 0" intent. The same rounding also turns 30-59.9 s into `"1m"` and 3599 s into `"60m"`, so the branch boundary is not handled cleanly either. The underlying JSON is unaffected, but the human text is the deliverable for these views and can report zero for a non-zero measured wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:14-18 (`dur`)

chunk_findings.detail: The early-return guard is evaluated *before* the "ready (dependencies done)" row is appended, so it tests for "at least two own events" rather than the "readiness alone is no story" condition its own comment describes. Given an item whose only own step is `lease.acquired` and whose span has a `ready_at` (i.e. the ordinary "claimed, still in flight / abandoned" case), `rows` holds exactly one entry, `rows[1:]` is empty, and the function returns `{"entries": [claim], "gaps": [], "biggest_gap": None, "total_s": None}` writing off the whole timeline. The `ready` marker is never added, so the ready→claim gap — precisely the queue wait the service advertises ("queue wait (ready->claimed)") and frequently the largest contributor to a slow item — is dropped, and the biggest gap is never named. Moving the ready append above the guard (or making the guard `if not rows`) yields `[ready, claim]`, one gap, and the correct `biggest_gap`/`total_s` for that same input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/retro.py:68 (`timeline`, guard `if not rows[1:]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `--phase` guard validates the phase name against `state.items`, the same mapping that the `retro` branch two blocks below validates an item id against (`if item not in state.items`). A single mapping cannot be keyed by both item ids (`B-rm-changes`) and workflow phase names (`build`, `docs`, …) unless every phase name happened to also be an item id, so at least one of the two checks is looking at the wrong collection. Concretely, `ddflow metrics --phase docs` (or `ddflow forecast --phase docs`) on a log that has plenty of items in the `docs` phase and no item literally named `docs` takes the line-76/77 branch and returns `Answer(False, "no phase 'docs'", failed=True)` — the command fails instead of filtering, so the whole `--phase` flag is unusable for every real phase name. The check needs to test against the set of phases actually present in `state` (e.g. `state.phases`, or the distinct `item.phase` values) rather than the item-id keyed `state.items`.

chunk_findings.detail: `reasons = Counter(" ".join(o.reason.split())[:100] or "(no reason)" for o in skipped)` calls `.split()` on the raw `o.reason` before the fallback can apply. The `or "(no reason)"` shows the author expects skips without a reason (the sibling `o.by or "(unknown)"` guards the same kind of missing field), but a missing reason is normally encoded as `None`, not `""`. Given a skip outcome with `reason=None` (a `gate skip` event logged with no justification — exactly the case the fallback is written for), `None.split()` raises `AttributeError` and the whole `ddflow metrics` skip audit aborts instead of tallying that skip under `"(no reason)"`; the fallback only ever fires for whitespace-only strings. The guard must be moved before the call, e.g. `(o.reason or "").split()`, so that missing reasons are bucketed rather than crashing the report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/skips.py:24 (`_gate_row`, the `reasons = Counter(...)` line)

chunk_findings.detail: `has_figures` decides exit 2 ("not enough data") by checking only `cycle_time`, `gate_time`, `review_rounds`, `rework`, `outcomes` and `providers`; it omits the two figures the same `build` computes into the returned dict: `queue_wait` and `lease_wait`. Its own docstring says "Whether any figure at all could be computed (else the answer is exit 2)", so this is self-inconsistent. Concrete input: a log where N ≥ `[metrics] min_samples` items have a dated `ready_at` and a `first_claim` (so `queue_waits(ctx)` yields N samples and `need("queue_wait", ...)` produces a real `p50_s`), but none of those items has completed (`cycle_s` is None, so `completed_spans` is empty) and no gate verdict has been recorded for them. Then `completed_spans`/`review_rounds` are empty, `gate_time`, `rework` and `outcomes` are all unavailable, and `has_figures` returns False, so the command exits 2 "not enough data" even though a computed queue-wait (and lease-wait) figure with sufficient samples exists in `data`. The same holds when the only supported figure is `lease_wait`. `has_figures` should also consult `data["queue_wait"]["p50_s"]` and `data["lease_wait"]["p50_s"]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py:has_figures
